question: How could a dry-zone inland capital become deeply integrated into Indian Ocean exchange?
mechanism: Engineered water storage supported dense settlement and agrarian production around Anuradhapura, while monastic and political institutions structured inland networks; the Malvatu Oya/Mantai corridor connected that inland system to a strategically placed north-western entrepôt serving Arabian Sea, Indian and Bay of Bengal circuits.
transmission_channel: water-managed agrarian hinterland → institutional/transport networks → north-west coastal gateway → multi-stage Indian Ocean exchange
time_lag: long-duration system across the Early Historic and Middle Historic periods; individual infrastructures and trade intensities changed substantially over time
scale: Z0 museum maps / observed landscape logic to Z2 inland polity and Z3 Indian Ocean system
confounders: local/monastic rather than purely royal water management
chronological compression in the museum maps
bounded_by: This bridge does not claim that irrigated surplus was the sole cause of maritime trade, that Mantai monopolized all exchange, or that the state centrally controlled the complete chain.
